data.comment:
Implementation complete, pushed to dev in commit 0281c93f (branch wl-LP-0MVECX47Z004LJAQ-adopted-llama-server-loses-its-log-sink).

## Root cause confirmed
spawn_and_capture() started llama-server with stdout=subprocess.PIPE plus a proxy-owned reader thread. On a proxy-only restart the new proxy ADOPTS the running backend but the reader thread died with the old proxy, leaving the pipe with writers only - llama-server.log froze indefinitely.

## Changes
1. AC1/AC5 - relay owned by the backend. spawn_and_capture() now redirects llama-server stdout/stderr DIRECTLY into llama-server.log (real file object passed as the child stdout). The write fd is held by the backend, so a proxy-only restart that adopts the backend keeps the log flowing with no re-attachment and no forced backend restart (warm prompt cache preserved). The legacy pipe relay is retained only when no real log file exists (DEVNULL/None).
2. AC2 - loud, never silent. _verify_adopted_log_relay() runs on every adoption: if the log exists but no process holds it open for writing (pre-fix pipe-based backend), it logs a WARNING and sets llama_log_source_unhealthy. It deliberately does NOT restart (AC5).
3. AC3 - observable freshness. GET /health now reports llama_log_age_seconds and llama_log_source_healthy. Write-only fd detection uses /proc/<pid>/fdinfo access-mode flags (read-only viewers/tailers are ignored) and excludes the proxy's own log handle.
4. Progress logging preserved. Extracted _ProgressLogger; prefill progress lines are now recovered by a llama-server.log tailer that follows rotation and is (re)started on adoption - so re-attachment is literal. start_llama_server() clears a stale unhealthy flag.
5. Tests: proxy/tests/test_log_relay_adoption.py (18 hermetic tests). Docs: proxy/README.md llama-server log section documents the durable relay and the new /health fields.

## Verification
- Full suite green at the pushed commit (run_tests.py --scope full): 0 failures.
- Ruff clean; refactor pipeline: 0 smells.
